observation.visible_scene: A close-up on a plain white surface showing two hands. The left hand grips a short black cylindrical object that has a through-hole at its upper end, and its index finger rests on a black disc/ring that encircles a long silver rod. The right hand pinches the far end of the same rod. A small, out-of-focus beige bead-like object sits in the background behind the left hand. The rod runs diagonally across the frame.
visible_changes: For the first ~15 frames the left index finger stays in contact with the black disc, which sits at the near (left) end of the rod; the rod's left tip is not visible beyond the disc.

The black disc then travels along the rod toward the end held by the right hand; as it does, the rod's left tip emerges on the far side of the disc and the exposed stub length grows (frames 16-30), while the left index finger lifts away from the disc (from about frame 24 onward).

The rod's orientation shifts from a nearly horizontal diagonal to a steeper diagonal with its left end raised, and the disc reaches the right-hand grip (around frames 29-33), after which it is largely hidden by the right fingers.
The left hand reorients/rotates the black cylinder so that its axial hole ends up facing the rod's left tip; in the final frames (34-41) the rod's left tip is aligned with and approaching that hole.
The right hand keeps holding the rod's far end throughout, with only small positional adjustments.
The beige background bead remains out of focus and roughly in place relative to the left hand.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rod is ultimately inserted into the black cylinder or withdrawn from it (the clip ends before any completion).
What the black cylinder and the beige bead are used for, and whether they are part of the same assembly.
The state of the disc/rod relationship before frame 1 and after frame 41.
uncertain_details: It is not determined from the frames alone whether the disc slides along a stationary rod or the rod is drawn through a held disc; both descriptions match the observed relative positions.
Camera motion is uncertain because the background is featureless; apparent position shifts of the hands/rod may include some camera movement.
Material identities (plastic, metal, 3D-printed, etc.) are not verifiable from the images.
